title: Scheduler tracing: split queueing vs compute time; add per-stage attributes and validation hooks
author: Julian Moore
release_notes: - Traces now attribute scheduler latency into queueing vs compute phases (no behavior change, observability-only).
body:
Title: Scheduler tracing: split queueing vs compute time; add per-stage attributes and validation hooks

Context
We’ve had multiple threads during profile pack bring-up where “scheduler latency” in traces was a single opaque bucket (and didn’t match the expected-behavior docs we’re writing for H100/L40S). This made it hard to tell whether p99 regressions were caused by queueing (admission control / backpressure / mixed workload) or actual GPU compute time.

This PR improves scheduler instrumentation to separate queueing vs compute time in traces, and attaches consistent attributes so dashboards can slice by profile_id / sku / workload_bucket without parsing logs.

Goals
- Make scheduler time attributable: queueing time vs compute time (prefill + decode)
- Align span naming + semantics across Hosted/Dedicated/Private (same runtime)
- Provide a lightweight validation hook used by perf-canary/benchmark-lab runs to assert that stage timing adds up (within tolerance) and catches missing spans

What changed
1) New trace spans (OpenTelemetry)
- request span (existing): runtime.request
- new child span: runtime.scheduler.queue
  - measures time from request entering scheduler to batch assignment / admission (including backpressure waits)
- new child span: runtime.scheduler.compute
  - measures scheduler-managed “compute window” for the request: time the request is part of an active batch until completion (includes GPU wait + execution; excludes explicit queue wait)
- new optional nested spans (best-effort; guarded by sampling)
  - runtime.scheduler.compute.prefill
  - runtime.scheduler.compute.decode

2) Attributes / tags (consistent across spans)
- runtime.profile_id (string)
- runtime.profile_version (string)
- runtime.gpu.sku (string; e.g. H100-SXM, H100-PCIe, L40S)
- runtime.scheduler.mode (string; e.g. mixed_len_v2)
- runtime.workload_bucket (string; short/medium/long context; derived from scheduler bucketing)
- runtime.model_family (string; llama, mistral, qwen, etc) (existing in some paths; normalized here)
- runtime.batch_id (string; low-cardinality stable ID per process; only emitted when trace sampled)

3) Metrics (low-cardinality counters/histograms)
- scheduler_queue_ms histogram (already added in earlier work; this PR standardizes name + emission location)
- scheduler_compute_ms histogram (new)
- scheduler_stage_mismatch_total counter (new)
  - increments when validation detects negative durations, missing timestamps, or stage sums outside tolerance

4) Validation hook (used in perf suites)
- Adds a debug-only assertion path behind RUNTIME_TRACE_VALIDATE_STAGES=1
- In perf-canary / benchmark-lab we enable it for sampled runs; in prod default is off
- Validation checks:
  - queue_ms >= 0, compute_ms >= 0
  - request_total_ms >= queue_ms + compute_ms - 2ms (clock tolerance)
  - if prefill/decode spans exist: compute_ms >= prefill_ms + decode_ms - 2ms

Why this is safe
- No scheduling logic changes; this is instrumentation-only
- Sampling rate unchanged; nested spans only emitted for sampled traces
- Attributes are restricted to low-cardinality values (explicitly avoided: request_id, prompt length, user/org identifiers)

Files / areas changed (high level)
- runtime/scheduler/tracing.{cc,h}
- runtime/scheduler/scheduler.{cc,h}
- runtime/observability/otel_helpers.{cc,h}
- runtime/metrics/scheduler_metrics.{cc,h}
- docs/internal/observability/tracing-conventions.md (updated naming/semantics)
- tests/runtime/scheduler_tracing_test.cc (new)

Testing
- Unit tests:
  - scheduler_tracing_test: verifies spans emitted, parent/child relationships, and attribute presence
  - stage_validation_test: synthetic timestamps validate mismatch counter behavior
- Local load test:
  - ran mixed prompt length workload (short+long) and confirmed p95 regressions can be attributed to queue_ms spikes
- CI:
  - runtime-unit: pass
  - runtime-integration: pass
  - lint/format: pass

Rollout / adoption
- This will land ahead of default profile pack rollout gates so SRE can use the new spans in incident triage.
- Expected behavior doc validation: once merged, we can update the H100/L40S expected-behavior pages to reference queue_ms vs compute_ms explicitly (instead of “scheduler latency”).

Related
- Linear: ENG-4924 (scheduler tuning), ENG-4931 (observability additions)
- Follow-ups:
  - Add trace exemplars linking scheduler_queue_ms histogram buckets to representative trace IDs (needs ingestion support)
  - Consider a single runtime.request.stage_breakdown attribute for non-trace metric consumers (optional)

Review notes / conversation
- Sofia Ivanova: Requested we define queue boundary precisely (“enqueue -> admitted into a batch”) and ensure compute excludes explicit queue wait. Addressed by taking queue timestamps at scheduler ingress and batch assignment, and compute timestamps at batch activation.
- Marcus Reed: Asked for a guard against attribute cardinality blowups (batch_id). Implemented: batch_id only when trace is sampled, and uses a per-process monotonic counter (no UUID).
- Allison Grant: Requested metric names align with dashboard spec (scheduler_queue_ms). Updated to standardize naming and added scheduler_compute_ms.
- Caleb Johnson: Requested attribute key normalization (runtime.gpu.sku vs gpu_sku). Updated keys and added a small helper to ensure consistent naming.

CI / checks
- Buildkite: runtime-linux-gpu (pass)
- Buildkite: runtime-linux-cpu (pass)
- Buildkite: clang-tidy (pass)
- Buildkite: unit-tests (pass)

Merge
Merged via squash merge into main.

Co-authored-by: Omar El-Sayed (review + metric naming alignment)
